--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.plot_traversal()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Render an interactive traversal visualization with a step-through slider. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.plot_traversal()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Render an interactive traversal visualization with a step-through slider. title: >- [Graph.plot_traversal()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Render an interactive traversal visualization with a step-through slider. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Render an interactive traversal visualization with a step-through slider. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4986-L5175){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.plot_traversal( visit_order=None, tree_edges=None, algorithm="", source=None, layout="force", theme=None, width=700, height=500, node_size=18.0, edge_width=1.5, show_labels=True, output=None, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Produces an HTML widget with an SVG graph and a slider control that steps through a BFS/DFS traversal one node at a time. Nodes transition through visual states: unvisited (gray), frontier (highlighted ring), current (bright glow), and visited (original color with step number). The visualization starts with every node unvisited and the start node on the frontier, then adds one node per step. At each step the node being visited is highlighted together with the tree edge used to reach it, visited nodes are numbered in visit order, and the frontier shows the unvisited neighbors of everything visited so far. Tree edges accumulate into the traversal tree as the slider advances. This is a teaching and debugging aid: it shows *how* a search explores a graph, which makes the difference between breadth-first (layer by layer) and depth-first (deep then backtrack) searches easy to see, and helps check which parts of a graph are reachable from a given node. Any visit order can be shown, so the output of a custom traversal can be visualized too. Unlike `play()`, which replays the graph's whole step log, this focuses on a single traversal and doesn't read the step log (when BFS is run automatically from `source=`, that search is recorded like any other `bfs()` call). Each node shows its label (or its ID if it has none), but the visit order must be expressed in node IDs (as returned by `bfs()` and `dfs()` with `return_list=True`). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [visit_order]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[list]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node IDs in traversal visit order, such as the list returned by `dfs(source, return_list=True)`. If `None` (default), `source=` must be provided and BFS is run automatically from it. Labels are not resolved here, so pass IDs. [tree_edges]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[list]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Explicit tree edges as `(source, target)` node ID pairs, where `target` is the node reached through that edge. If `None` (default) and BFS is run from `source=`, the edges BFS followed are used. Otherwise they are inferred from the visit order by attaching each node to an already-visited neighbor (on directed graphs, a predecessor, since the tree edge must point to the node): the earliest-visited one when `algorithm=` starts with `"BFS"` (the BFS parent), else the most recently visited one (the DFS parent). [algorithm]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[""]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Label shown in the controls (e.g., `"BFS"`, `"DFS"`). Default is `""`, which shows no label, except when BFS is run automatically from `source=`, in which case it becomes `"BFS"`. [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Starting node (ID or label). Only used when `visit_order=` is `None`, in which case BFS is run from this node. Default is `None`. [layout]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["force"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Layout algorithm: `"force"` (default, force-directed), `"circular"`, or `"random"` (see `seed=`), or the name of a node attribute holding `(x, y)` positions, such as the `"pos"` attribute the `layout_*()` methods set (see `plot()`). Any other value raises `ValueError`. [theme]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Color theme: `"auto"`, `"light"` or `"dark"`, which also selects the colors used for the unvisited, frontier, current and visited states. `"auto"` follows the color scheme of the page showing the widget, or else the system's (see `plot()`). If `None` (default), the widget is `"auto"` on screen and light in saved files. Any other value raises `ValueError`. [width]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[700]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : SVG canvas width in pixels. Default is `700`. [height]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[500]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : SVG canvas height in pixels. Default is `500`. [node_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[18.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node circle radius in pixels, applied to every node. Default is `18.0`. [edge_width]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.5]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edge stroke width in pixels. Default is `1.5`. [show_labels]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to display node labels. Default is `True`. [output]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional file path to save to. A path ending in `.html` saves the interactive widget; any other extension saves only the static SVG. Default is `None` (nothing is saved). [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the `"force"` and `"random"` layouts. The same seed on the same graph gives the same positions. If `None` (default), positions differ between calls. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [StepPlayer]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Interactive traversal visualization with step-through slider, node state transitions, and visit-order numbering. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If neither `visit_order=` nor `source=` is provided. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~play`) : Replay the whole step log, traversals included. [](`~bfs`) : The breadth-first search run from source=. [](`~dfs`) : A depth-first visit order to pass as visit_order=. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Passing just `source=` runs a breadth-first search from that node. On the metro map, drawn at its stored positions, the search from Central reaches the four stations next to it first, then the stations two stops away, and so on outward. Step through the slider to see the frontier (the ringed nodes) move out from the center: ::: {#a4590ab0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec metro = ec.metro() metro.plot_traversal(source="Central", layout="pos") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
Step 0 / 20
BFS traversal — 20 nodes
``` ::: ::: ### Depth first To show a different traversal, compute the visit order yourself and name it with `algorithm=`. A depth-first search from Central follows one branch as far as it goes before backing up to try another, so it reaches Hillcrest, four stops out, on its fifth visit: ::: {#ec591e9a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} order = metro.dfs("Central", return_list=True) metro.plot_traversal(visit_order=order, algorithm="DFS", layout="pos") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
Step 0 / 20
DFS traversal — 20 nodes
``` ::: ::: ### Any visit order The visit order can come from anywhere. Ordering the stations by travel time from Westgate, and attaching each one to the station before it on its fastest route, shows Dijkstra's algorithm at work. It reaches stations in order of minutes rather than stops, so Riverside, three quick stops away (10 minutes), comes before Northpark, two slow stops away (11 minutes): ::: {#a527ec66 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} minutes = metro.single_source_shortest_path_length( "Westgate", return_dict=True ) paths = metro.single_source_shortest_path("Westgate") order = sorted(minutes, key=minutes.get) tree = [(path[-2], path[-1]) for path in paths.values() if len(path) > 1] metro.plot_traversal( visit_order=order, tree_edges=tree, algorithm="Dijkstra", layout="pos" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
Step 0 / 20
Dijkstra traversal — 20 nodes
``` ::: ::: To replay a traversal along with everything else that happened to a graph, use `play()` instead: it shows each `bfs()` or `dfs()` call in the step log one visited node at a time.
